It is 9:12 pm here in Ithaca, New York. I just finished sending a voice memo to my partner about *Ribes*. When I get talking about gooseberries I can help but think about *Ribes aureum*. One of the first scientific names I had down pat. This species is planted all around Colorado College’s campus and one of the first plants we were taking to in field botany.   

![ribes aureum at the aviary disc golf course (inaturalist.org/observations/158628931)](images/ribes-disc.jpg)
I do not mean to go on a tangent about *Ribes* so I will leave it at that for now. I really wanted to make a blog post because I think the only person who reads this blog is my friend David Flynn. He always gets on me for not posting on here enough so this one (and every one so far in some way) is for you. 

![its becoming a tradition](images/flynnsgiving-2025.jpeg)
I feel like an update in my graduate studies is due. So much has happened since my last post on August 27th, 2025. I have completed field work in Florida, Belize, Texas and Panama in that order and in a week will be heading to Honduras to visit the Paul Stanley Herbarium and geek out and collect some *Catopsis*.
 
 
I am really blessed to be supported by a variety of grants and more importantly an amazing community of folks who unbeknownst have become the energy of a wave to keep me going in my studies. I want to thank Cole Luttrel, Ella Baron and Ramon daPena for their support logistically in the field. On top of that, I must say thanks for the laughter and fun while out looking for *Catopsis.*

I am feeling pretty emotional right now, for better or for worse, I have been going about my work and life in silence. My emotions have felt to heavy to listen to music, and the feelings and focus I have had during those moments without music has slowly crept into my time in the lab.
 
 

So really why am I writing this blog post right now? Because I wanted to write down that I shed a good amount of tears looking at photos of my late cat Buddy Guy. The tears came from this feeling of wishing I had the want for emotional intimacy I have done my fair share of looking back at old photos trying to find similar photographs like above of *Ribes aureum.* Now in my 4th year of my phd I feel old, I feel happy that the hortorium is in a renaissance, I feel wise and sad that I wish I had the emotional intimacy as I think I could have tackled so many more additional things during my phd if I had realized this sooner. I still have time so I am happy it occurred this August to the present day.

![i love you forever and always buddy guy.](buddy-guy.jpeg)
